players.product: EDA software and chip design simulation tools accelerated by NVIDIA CUDA

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Q4 FY2026 targets: total revenue between $2.53 billion and $2.58 billion; GAAP costs and expenses between $2.225 billion and $2.3 billion; non-GAAP costs and expenses between $1.45 billion and $1.48 billion; GAAP EPS $0.60-$0.85 and non-GAAP EPS $4.10-$4.16. Management expects double-digit organic EDA revenue growth in Q4 and for the full year 2026 and continues to expect the IP business to grow sequentially in Q4. Full-year GAAP EPS is guided to $3.84-$4.08 and GAAP costs and expenses to $8.667 billion-$8.742 billion, including an increase in expected fiscal 2026 restructuring charges as the company accelerates its committed synergies.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $2.53 billion-$2.58 billion; Q4 non-GAAP EPS $4.10-$4.16

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 cash and cost execution: free cash flow was $746 million and cash and short-term investments ended the quarter at $3.6 billion. Total non-GAAP costs and expenses were $1.446 billion, at the lower end of the guided range; CFO: the company is ahead of schedule on the Ansys cost synergy commitments made at close.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 free cash flow $746 million; cash and short-term investments $3.6 billion

quarterly_data.signal: ANSYS one year in: CEO said Ansys continues to see strong demand 'From semis to aerospace to industrial and more'; a leading automaker is using Ansys SimAI to achieve roughly 98% prediction accuracy and move crash analysis to near real-time, and a leading heavy equipment manufacturer achieved more than 10x faster motor design. CFO: 'we are seeing strength in the Ansys business, including the channel business'; the Ansys revenue contribution guide was raised $20 million to approximately $2.98 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: SimAI roughly 98% prediction accuracy; more than 10x faster motor design

quarterly_data.signal: IP FACTORY TWO business model: CEO said every hyperscaler is investing in and at various stages of delivering its own custom silicon, and 'These chips will not happen without our interface IP'; Synopsys is 'in advanced discussions with number of these customers to change the business model from the traditional IP license plus some NRE to a license plus a royalty', to be modelled at the Investor Day. Security IP is one of the growth areas behind the Processor IP divestiture (not split out separately); CEO: 'we have a great market position in security'.

MULTIPHYSICS FUSION adoption: CEO said customers in the early engagements have validated the joint Synopsys-Ansys solution and are 'in early stages of deployment'; 'The moment we move to production, which those customers will move to production, we'll start seeing the revenue upside.' On budgets: 'even if it is coming from an EDA budget, the joint solution will capture an upside in revenue to the existing separate point tools.' Leading customers are requiring thermal, structure and stress to be taken into account during design implementation of 3DIC architectures. CEO on EDA software: 'We're very happy with the software component, actually. Very, very pleased.'
